text:
Aisha: Quick thread to agree on an Optimize Advisor pilot playbook. Goal: deliver batching/caching/quant recommendations + eval-triggered alerts with clear safety nets. I sketched a lightweight plan, pls react.

Ben: Love it. High-level ask: we need two parallel pilots: one for chat-heavy (low-latency) and one for embeddings/async (throughput). Different acceptance criteria.

Chen: Agreed. Sketch for metrics:
- chat pilot: p50/p95 latency impact < +10ms, semantic loss < 0.5% (task-specific), token savings >= 12%
- embed pilot: throughput uplift or cost reduction >= 18%, recall/embedding-similarity delta < 0.75%
Also require eval-trigger config as a first-class object.

Diego: Ops constraints: pilot should run on Dedicated + one Private customer (if they opt in). Must include fast rollback (feature-flag + per-tenant kill switch). Canary schedule: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with observability checks between steps.

Elena: From customers: they want a preview flow that shows expected savings and a short bullet "why this rec" (e.g., "high prefix reuse -> batching" or "stable embeddings -> 8-bit quant OK"). Also they want an audit trail and opt-out per model.

Frank: Prioritization: propose a simple scorecard for picking pilots: expected monthly $ savings, product risk (high/med/low), technical feasibility (0-3), and strategic value (customer ARR). We'll weight savings 35%, risk 35%, feasibility 20%, strategic 10%.

Grace: On explainability: we should produce a one-line reason + small diagnostic snippet (e.g., top-k similar cache hits, median sequence length, per-token entropy) so customers can decide. That snippet can be used in the preview UI.

Aisha: Pilot gates (proposal):
- Enrollment: explicit opt-in from customer; signed A/B pilot agreement
- Safety: no customer-facing regression exceeding thresholds in Chen's metrics for the pilot window (14d)
- Observability: tracing and token-level cost attribution enabled for pilot tenants
- Rollback threshold: if >2 P1/P2 incidents or quality regression > set thresholds, immediate rollback

Ben: Runtime work items: adaptive batching must honor per-tenant concurrency and not elevate p99 beyond SLO. I'll add an integration test to simulate 10x burst and validate autoscale + batching latency behavior.

Chen: Eval-trigger example (draft) for review:
```
trigger_name: advisor_eval_simple
min_samples: 600
lookback_days: 14
metrics:
  - name: app_quality_metric
    comparator: absolute_drop
    threshold: 0.005
  - name: token_savings
    comparator: relative_gain
    threshold: 0.12
actions:
  - notify: product@redwood.com
  - rollback: automatic_if_drop>0.02
```

Diego: Infra note: caching recommendations must include TTL guidance and eviction priority. For Private deployments we need to document encryption-at-rest and KMS integration. I'll draft a short infra runbook.

Elena: I'll shortlist 4 customers and map them to the two pilot lanes. Preference: small set of high-traffic customers who can commit to logs and an SRE point-of-contact. I'll DM owners.

Frank: I'll build the prioritization sheet and tag top 3 candidates by score. We can pick the final 2 from there.

Grace: UX ask: preview UI should be minimal for Pilot (email + sandbox link), Beta should add an in-console preview with estimated tradeoffs and an 'apply' button.

deploy-bot: CI passed for branch=optimize/advisor-playbook commit=7c1b2a -> staging. 9/9 checks green.

Aisha: Next steps and owners: 1) Ben write autoscale test harness (due Wed), 2) Chen finalize eval-trigger configs + tests (due Wed), 3) Diego publish infra runbook + rollback checklist (due Thu), 4) Elena confirm pilot customers (due Thu), 5) Frank share prioritization sheet (due Tue). We'll meet Fri 11am to lock pilots. If no objections, we adopt these gates.

Ben: ack, will start on harness.

Chen: ack, will iterate on thresholds after we see initial variance.

Diego: ack, will include KMS notes.

Elena: ack, will DM the list by EOD Thu.

Frank: ack, sheet incoming Tue morning.

Aisha: Thanks team. If folks want to add pilot-specific tweaks (e.g., longer lookback for low-traffic customers), raise them in the Fri huddle. :rocket:
